_comment: v3.0 declarative starting point. Delete every _comment key. See FORMAT.md.
_comment_timeGrid: slotMinutes must divide 1440. 15 represents 08:30/15:30/06:30 exactly; 60 cannot represent any half-hour. Fewer slots = smaller model.
_comment_calendar: weekStart may be any of the 7 days; it defines the weeks that per-week limits are counted over. Marking a holiday lets it carry its own demand in demand.csv -- it does NOT make anyone unavailable. hasEve says the day before is its eve, so that day can carry its own demand too; the eve's date needs no stating.
_comment_employees: One list for both models. contractAssignments and teamAssignments are date-ranged: multiple, possibly discontinuous, must not overlap (per team). end: null = ongoing. LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST.
_comment_demand: workPeriods are DEMAND BUCKETS, not a menu of shifts. They say where coverage is wanted and, together, delimit the operating window. A worker works a contiguous block of their contracted length anywhere inside it.

demand._comment_priorityOrder: Which team/level combinations get filled first. Sort by `order`, first match wins; a bare {team} matches any level, add `level` to name one exactly. Anything unlisted sorts last, tied. Ordering follows `order`, NOT array position, so you can rearrange these freely. Remember level 1 is the HIGHEST, so {team, level: 1} means that team's most senior. Needs usePriorityOrder.

_comment_scheduleInput: Every declared code must also be classified under dayOffCodes; leaving one unclassified is an error, not a default.

markingTypes.DO: Day off - may be swapped, at a penalty
markingTypes.FDO: Forced day off - cannot be changed

_comment_constraints: hard[] carries ONLY what nothing else can express -- min_rest_minutes is currently the sole type. Coverage, day-off penalties and skill priority are objectives, not rules; day-off classification is dayOffCodes; contract limits are on the contract. `type` is enumerated, so a typo is an error, not a silent no-op. `scope` is reserved for v3.1 per-employee rules and only accepts "global".
_comment_optimization: Use `algorithm` for one run, or `pipeline: [...]` for phases (exactly one of the two). demandInterpretation is where hard/soft is decided, per phase -- the demand data itself takes no position. `goal` is one of MathematicalDefinition7's three objective functions.
